title: Per-domain specialists x data scaling (A5 x M116): do routed specialists' per-domain Q_d(n) curves rise at least as steeply as the global arm's?

device._note: HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1, gfx1201; whitening and ridge on numpy CPU; frozen per-domain encode on GPU.

parity_guard.feature: CLS token concatenated with the mean of the patch tokens

sparse.specialist_construction: A5 exact: per-domain random whitened-patch candidates (seed [11, domain], n_cap 20000), atoms picked by the seeded permutation
sparse.head: closed_form_ridge_1.0
sparse._note: fixed 512 atoms per domain (disclosed): the question is the SHAPE of per-domain Q_d(n), not A5's per-domain budget allocation

scaling.subsample_rule: first n rows of each domain's train rows (corpus order, nested)
scaling.test_set: each domain's FULL test rows, identical for every ladder point
scaling.global_baseline: M116 sealed sparse per-domain accuracy (global 3072 arm) over its global ladder - the baseline steepness per domain
scaling._note: a specialist sees n rows of ITS domain; the global arm at global n sees ~n/6 rows of that domain. The gate compares GAINS over each arm's own ladder (steepness of per-domain accuracy vs per-domain data), which is the scale-fair quantity.

gate.kill_switch_specialist_steepness: fired if any domain's specialist per-domain gain Q_d(n_full) - Q_d(n_first) is < 0.5 x the global arm's per-domain gain over M116's ladder for that domain
gate.reported: per-domain specialist curves, per-domain global curves (M116), gains, ratios, and the head-to-head at full data (A5's per-domain cost win, re-checked at full data)
